chunks: And from him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali Al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gives the servant from the reward for good manners just as He gives to the fighter in the Way of Allah, morning and evening.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for having good manners in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni places this narration within the chapter on good manners to establish that ethical refinement is not merely social etiquette but a profound act of worship comparable to the continuous striving (jihad) of the battlefield. This comparison elevates the status of the believer who maintains patience and grace in daily interactions, suggesting that moral discipline requires the same sustained effort and yields equal divine reward as physical sacrifice in the path of Allah. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner character with outward action as a complete path to spiritual excellence.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali Al Lahby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having sid:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would be Giving from the Rewards to the servant based upon the good manners, just as He<sup>azwj</sup> would Give to the fighter in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (waking up) in the morning and going upon it’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim from Ali ibn abu Ali al-Lahabi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘

Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, grants good rewards to a person of excellent moral behavior as He grants rewards to one who strives hard (does Jihad) in the way of Allah, mornings and evenings.’”
